instruction: I went on a trip with friends to Maui recently. I have maintained a note of money I owe to others and others owe me from the trip in simple note. Make private venmo payments or requests accordingly. In the payments/requests, add a note, "For Maui trip".
notes: The note is found via simple_note.search_notes(query='Maui') and read via show_note; its content (world state) is encoded as static i-owe / owes-me facts gated by the knowledge predicate (note-read). Friends are placeholders: the exact number and split is only known after reading the note; the model assumes two friends Brenda owes (-> venmo.create_transaction) and two who owe her (-> venmo.create_payment_request), each private with description 'For Maui trip'. Friend emails are resolved from the names in the note with venmo.search_friends (known-email); if the note already lists emails those lookups are redundant but harmless. The note, friends, amounts, description and privacy flag are declared as domain constants so supervisor-complete-task can state the full goal conjunction as its precondition without extra parameters; credentials, tokens, queries and emails are problem objects. Every non-final action requires (not (task-completed)), so complete_task is necessarily last. Answer is not required (no question asked).

plan: (venmo-create-transaction email-friend-1 amount-i-owe-friend-1 simple-note-token desc-for-maui-trip private-true friend-1 note-maui-trip)
(venmo-create-transaction email-friend-2 amount-i-owe-friend-2 simple-note-token desc-for-maui-trip private-true friend-2 note-maui-trip)
(venmo-create-payment-request email-friend-3 amount-friend-3-owes-me simple-note-token desc-for-maui-trip private-true friend-3 note-maui-trip)
(venmo-create-payment-request email-friend-4 amount-friend-4-owes-me simple-note-token desc-for-maui-trip private-true friend-4 note-maui-trip)
